final_answer: The computational complexity of the attack on AES-256 by Alex Biryukov, Orr Dunkelman, Nathan Keller, Dmitry Khovratovich, and Adi Shamir is 239, 245, or 270 times for 9, 10, or 11 rounds respectively. AES-256 has computational security against brute-force attacks, as the best attack using their technique on AES with a 128-bit key requires storing more data than all the data stored on all the computers on the planet in 2016, making it impractical.
